claims.claim: Reviewers describe the visuals as featuring pixel art graphics combined with shader work and scan lines.

citations.review_text:
It's Balatro... 
Basically, it's too late for me to write an in depth review, since it defined an entire new genre but I'll still try to describe it in brief.
Simple yet quite well made pixel art graphics paired with excellent shader work and sound design, a game loop based on reaching ever-increasing goals each round. It just so happens that the playing pieces are regular poker cards, and yet they're whimsy-fied with new crazy mechanics layered on top.

It's a blast. Also, the sheer amount of great and mathematically sound content in this is enough for me to recommend it to just about anyone.

I bought this game due to the hype. I worry that leaving a negative review is a little harsh, but this game is a global smash hit, so I guess it won't hurt the devs too badly. This is just the cautionary review that I wish I had read before buying.

This is just a card game with some fancy mechanics. The graphics are pretty nice, but at the end of the day they're just fancy cards with scan lines and '90s effects. The mechanics seem to go very deep, and some people apparently get hooked by this and spend hours and hours playing into the night.

I just don't care about card games. It's too dry and abstract for me. Other deckbuilders dress things up with dungeons, monsters or what have you. Here there's none of that. Okay, there are some zany card designs, and recreations of childhood card collection aesthetics such as holographic or metallic cards. It reminds me of Pogs or something. I was never into collectible cards as a kid, maybe that's the problem.

It's not a terrible game. And I love to see an indie developer succeed. Good on em. But I just don't care about cards.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game combines poker mechanics with card-modding elements like tarot cards, planet cards, and changeable deck cards.

citations.review_text: This game is very good and a masterpiece. The way you can "cheat" your way through poker with tarot cards and you can upgrade the hands with planet cards or simply add/remove cards from your deck with legitimate game mechanics is amazing. And there's a speedrun community as well! 10/10

At first, I shrugged this off as some kind of gimmicky game. But when I finally decided to try it, I have become amazed at how such a simple-looking game can transform into something incredibly complex. The game is all about modifying the score and building up enough chips to beat the blinds. The Joker and card-modding system that is part of this game helps you do just that. However, only the right combination of jokers, modded cards, and alterations to card play levels will help you succeed.

Suddenly, what seems to be what looks like a simple game becomes an act of "just one more try". It pulled me in, and it's got a hold on me.

Seriously, give it a try. It's often cheap, and once you understand how the scoring system works, the only thing you'll be wondering is "how to best make number go up" each and every time. It's not just poker. It's poker where you [i]bend the rules.[/i]

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Players enjoy the diverse decks and deep strategic depth as challenges ramp up.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game includes multiple decks, challenges, and unlockable jokers that provide varied strategies and replayability.

citations.review_text: Absolutely addictive, I own it on my iPad too and probably have around as many hours on there as steam. Easy to understand and get started but the game has lot to unlock and challenge yourself later. Deserves all the praise and hype it got.

[b]Balatro[/b] is a poker-inspired roguelike deckbuilder where you combine traditional poker hands with a variety of special cards to create increasingly higher-scoring combinations. The core gameplay is simple, but there's a surprising amount of strategy involved in managing your deck, choosing the right Jokers, and figuring out how to maximize your score. Every run comes with different possibilities, and finding a combination that turns an otherwise mediocre deck into an unstoppable scoring machine never gets old.

A big part of what makes Balatro so engaging is its progression curve. The early game is all about managing your limited resources and trying to stay afloat, while the right combination of Jokers and upgrades can eventually turn things around and make your score snowball out of control. There's also plenty of variety between the different decks and challenges, giving you new restrictions and opportunities to experiment with different strategies. The retro-inspired theme ties everything together, making the game feel like something straight out of an old Windows card game collection.

Despite all the strategic depth, Balatro is also very accessible. Runs are easy to pick up and play in short sessions, and the game never engages in modern monetization gimmicks like shops or battle passes. The fact that it has a clear stopping point at Ante 8 while still allowing you to push further into Endless mode is another nice touch, giving each run a concrete objective without taking away the option to see how far your build can go.

Overall, Balatro is an incredible roguelike deckbuilder - managing your economy, experimenting with different builds, and gradually turning a struggling run into a powerful one is very satisfying. It can get repetitive over longer sessions, but as long as you don't fall for the excessive hype around it you'll have a great time. It's an easy recommendation for anyone who enjoys card games and roguelikes with strategic depth.
